tips.cheekR: Double-click the wood to reset the window to 100%. Try: resize the window, then double-click here.
tips.brand: Pawltec by Studio 87. A free, open source tube-style program equalizer. Try: open About & Support for the project links.
tips.pPrev: Previous preset ([ key). Steps back through the list. Try: tap it to audition factory sounds quickly.
tips.pName: Open the preset browser. Double-click to rename your own preset. Try: click it, search for "trick", and load Low Trick 60.
tips.pNext: Next preset (] key). Steps forward through the list. Try: tap it to audition factory sounds quickly.
tips.pSave: Save these settings as your own preset. Asks before overwriting. Try: tweak a factory sound, then save your own version.
tips.bBypass: Bypass: hear the dry signal to compare with the equalized sound (B key). The meters keep moving. Try: switch it during playback and match the loudness by ear.
tips.bGuide: Short guide and keyboard shortcuts. Try: read the low trick note first.
tips.bSettings: Info bubbles, power saving, colour look. Try: switch between the three looks.
tips.bAbout: About Pawltec, support and where your files live. Try: open it to find the project links.
tips.cvResp: What the equalizer does to each frequency, in dB. The thick line is the total; the thin lines are the four sections. Drag a round handle up or down to change that section, or sideways to pick another frequency. Hover to read a value. Hover to read frequency, note, EQ gain and spectrum level. Try: drag the low handles to the same spot for the low trick.
tips.cvSpec: Live spectrum of the preview sound. Grey line: before the equalizer. Coloured fill: after it. Scale is dB below full level. Hover to read frequency, note, and level. Small labels name the strongest peaks. Try: play pink noise and watch the curve shape it.
tips.cvMet: Level of the sound going in and coming out, in dB. Blue is safe, purple is the warning zone, pink is clipping. Click to clear the clip lights. Try: keep the loudest peaks in the purple zone and out of pink.

groups.title: Low section
groups.tip: Low section: boost and atten share one frequency. Try: use Boost and Atten here together for the low trick.

cells.tip: Low frequency: 20, 30, 60 or 100 Hz. Sets where both the low boost and the low atten work. Click a number, drag, or use the wheel. Try: 60 Hz for kick and bass, 30 Hz for sub.

Low boost: lifts the bass around the chosen low frequency, up to +13.5 dB. 0 does nothing. Try: Boost and Atten together on the same low frequency, the famous low end trick, for a fat bump without mud.

Low atten: turns the lows down, up to -17.5 dB. Use it with Boost on the same frequency for the classic trick: a fat bump with a clean dip just above it. Try: raise Boost on the same frequency too, the famous low end trick, so the bass gets big and the mud above it gets cleaned.

groups.title: High boost
groups.tip: High boost: a bell you can make narrow or wide. Try: start with 2 to 4 on the boost.

cells.tip: High boost frequency: 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 12 or 16 kHz. This is the centre of the high boost bell. Try: 3 or 4 kHz for punch, 10 to 16 kHz for air.
High boost: lifts the highs around the chosen frequency, up to +18 dB. Use Bandwidth to make it narrow or wide. Try: small amounts, 2 to 4, for air on vocals and cymbals.
Bandwidth of the high boost. 0 is narrow and pointed, 10 is wide and gentle. Wide settings sound smooth and natural. Try: wide (7 to 10) for a smooth lift, narrow (0 to 3) to pick out one spot.

groups.title: High atten
groups.tip: High atten: turns the highs down above a corner frequency. Try: start at 5 kHz or 10 kHz.

cells.tip: High atten frequency: 5, 10 or 20 kHz. Above this point the highs are turned down smoothly. Try: 5 kHz to calm harshness, 20 kHz for a gentle top trim.
High atten: turns the highs down above the chosen frequency, up to -16 dB. Good for taming harshness and hiss. Try: 1 to 3 to soften a bright source or hide hiss.

groups.title: Tube stage
groups.tip: Tube stage and output level. Try: 2 to 3 on Tube, then adjust Output.

cells.tip: Tube stage warmth: adds soft, tube-like colour and gentle peak rounding. 0 is clean and bit-exact. Preview only uses a simple model. Try: 2 to 4 to add warmth to a clean sound.

Output level after the equalizer. 5 is 0 dB, range -12 to +12 dB. Boosting makes things sound better just because they are louder, so match levels when you compare. Try: match the level with Bypass on and off before judging.
